topic: Unlocking Planar Graph Duality and Euler's Characteristic Formula
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
lecture_lines: Planar graphs have no crossing edges.
Vertices, edges, and faces define the structure.
Faces include the unbounded outer region.
animations: Draw four edges forming a square, colored #FFD700.
Add a label V for the vertex, and E for edges, color #FFD700.

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula states V minus E plus F equals 2.
This formula holds for any connected planar graph.
V is vertices, E is edges, F is faces.
animations: Write the V - E + F = 2 formula in #FFFFFF.
Display a connected planar graph example.
Animate V, E, and F labels with colors #00FF00, #FF0000, #0000FF.

sections.title: Concept of the Dual Graph
lecture_lines: Dual graphs place vertices inside each face.
Edges connect vertices of adjacent faces.
This creates a new linked structure.
animations: Place dots in each face of the primal graph.
Connect dots through adjacent faces in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Deep Dive: The Duality Relationship
lecture_lines: Duality preserves edges but swaps vertices and faces.
V star equals F, F star equals V.
E star equals E holds perfectly.
animations: Display equation V' = F and F' = V in #FFFFFF.
Animate swapping vertex/face roles with highlight.
Finalize the duality map visualization with labels.

sections.title: Summary and Application
lecture_lines: It aids circuit design and map coloring.
Use duality for efficient routing pathways.
animations: Flash the V' = F, E' = E relationships.
Simulate a map coloring problem, shifting face colors.
